messages:
Sam: opening a PRD intake for a small feature we've had a lot of inbound asks about — 'Response Consistency Gate'.
Sam: problem statement: customers observe nondeterministic answers across retries, model rollouts, and small prompt variations. for compliance use-cases this causes weird audit gaps. want a configurable gate to flag or block responses that deviate from an expected canonical answer set.
Sam: goals: (1) detect cross-response divergence for pinned prompt sets; (2) provide two enforcement modes — alert-only (soft) and block-with-fallback (hard); (3) expose per-customer thresholds and telemetry.
Sam: non-goals: this is not a hallucination fixer, not a model-training effort, and not realtime semantic reconciliation.
Sam: proposed success metrics: stable-response-ratio >= 95% on customer pinned prompts; false-block rate < 1%; end-to-end latency increase <= 50ms p50 when gate enabled.
Mike: quick Q — how do we define "deviation"? exact-match? semantic similarity?
Ana: +1 on that. need concrete acceptance criteria, otherwise eng can't implement. also streaming behavior matters.
Sam: thinking: multilayered checks: (a) token-level/n-gram overlap for deterministic templates, (b) semantic similarity embedding score for freeform (cosine >= 0.88 default), (c) configurable whitelist for acceptable variance.
Sam: acceptance criteria (draft):
```
1) Gate can be toggled per-customer and per-route.
2) For template prompts, exact-match path supported.
3) For freeform prompts, system computes embedding similarity; if score < threshold, action according to enforcement mode.
4) Gate exposes logs with original response, alternative candidates, similarity score, and decision reason.
5) End-to-end latency with gate enabled must stay within +50ms p50 vs baseline for typical 512-token requests.
6) Automated eval harness runs 10k pinned prompts and reports stable-response-ratio and false-block rate.
```
Sheila: edge-cases to call out: function-calling responses (structure may differ but semantically same), streaming tokens (partial similarity hard), multimodal contexts (we may not support yet).
Jordan: for rollout: suggest canary 1% -> 5% -> 25% with automated rollback if stable-response-ratio drops >2pt vs baseline. also need eval-suites from CS for top 3 customers to run gated tests.
Ana: on streaming: maybe we only run the gate after finalization (end-of-stream) for streaming endpoints. for ultra-low-latency routes we could offer async post-check + alert-only.
Mike: implementation questions: where does this live? eng-runtime or a middleware in front of runtime? my preference: lightweight middleware in front so we can short-circuit to fallback model variants without changing runtime kernels.
Sam: agree middleware makes sense to start. eng-runtime can later adopt optimized paths for tight-latency customers.
Sheila: we need to enumerate fallback strategies: (a) regenerate on same model up to N times; (b) fallback to pinned canonical answer if provided; (c) route to human review for flagged enterprise flows.
Sam: good list — add to PRD. also need UX for CS: a per-customer dashboard showing examples, rates, and the ability to mark false positives (whitelist).
Jordan: timeline ask from sales: can we commit to alpha for 2 enterprise pilots in 6 weeks? Feels tight but doable if scope is limited: alert-only + dashboard + eval-harness.
Sam: proposal: alpha = alert-only + dashboard + eval-harness + 2 pilot customers. beta = add block-mode + fallback strategies + canary rollout infra.
Ana: acceptance criteria tweak: include explicit tests for function-calls and streaming finalization.
Sam: noted. who's volunteering to own the PRD write-up and the RFC? @Mike for implementation notes, @Ana for acceptance test plan, @Jordan to coordinate pilot customers, @Sheila for edge-case matrix, I'll own success metrics + rollout policy.
Mike: I can draft the RFC next week, will ping infra and eng-runtime for feasibility checks.
Sheila: I'll build the edge-case table and list open questions for security/PII impacts.
Jordan: I'll loop in CS and two pilot contacts, and get their pinned prompt sets.
Sam: eval-bot: can you run an initial pass on a small synthetic prompt set to give a baseline stable-response-ratio for gptlike-open-variants?
eval-bot: baseline run (synthetic 500 prompts): stable-response-ratio = 86.4%, mean similarity = 0.76, median latency delta with naive post-check = +68ms. (preliminary)
Sam: ok parity check — we need to get that similarity up and latency down. next steps: draft PRD doc with above ACs, post RFC draft in #eng-platform, schedule a 30m sync next Tue. :calendar: :eyes: 
Mike: :thumbsup:
Ana: thanks, putting this in my queue.
Sheila: noted, will add security questions.
